identification.title: All My Ways Are Known to You
identification.notes: Written by Michael Farren, Dustin Smith, Jonny Robinson and Rich Thompson; copyright 2016 CityAlight Music, Farren Love And War Publishing and Integrity's Alleluia! and Praise! Music, administered by Capitol CMG Publishing; CCLI 7073327. The list's guess of CityAlight is right for the recording churches know (album Only a Holy God, released 2017). The copyright year is 2016 and the album year 2017. Reviewed as the song, not any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: Three verses, a short chorus ending in a hallelujah, and a closing tag praying for opened eyes. Verses 1 and 2 are addressed to God and set out his knowledge of the believer's path and his providence; verse 3 faces death. The song speaks of God's providence only: the incarnation, cross, resurrection and return are not mentioned, and neither Christ nor the Spirit is named.

claims.claim: God knows the believer's whole path, in every circumstance, whether peace or loss, wealth or poverty.
claims.subject: God's omniscience

claims.claim: No trial lies beyond God's hand and no step is outside his plan; he knows the way even in darkness.
claims.subject: Providence and sovereignty

claims.claim: The believer can have peace wherever he is, because God knows his ways.
claims.subject: Peace and assurance

claims.claim: Death need not be feared, since it is the door to life and God takes the believer's hand and leads him through.
claims.subject: Hope beyond death

claims.claim: The singer prays for eyes to see that God made the path and walks it with him.
claims.subject: God's presence and guidance

strengths.title: God's knowledge and care over every circumstance
strengths.explanation: The song rests the believer's peace on who God is: he knows every step, no trial exceeds his hand, and nothing falls outside his plan. That is doctrine taught about God, and the comfort is grounded in it rather than in the singer's feelings.
strengths.scriptureRationale: God searching and knowing every way of the psalmist.

strengths.title: Trials kept within God's limits
strengths.explanation: No trial is beyond God's hand, which matches the teaching that God does not let his people be tested beyond what they can bear.
strengths.scriptureRationale: God is faithful and does not allow testing beyond what the believer can bear.

strengths.title: Death met with God's guiding hand
strengths.explanation: The third verse treats death as the door to life with God leading through it, echoing the valley of the shadow of death, though it does not name Christ's resurrection as the ground.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Walking through the valley without fear because God is present.

doctrinesAffirmed: Peace and assurance in God's care
theological.assessment: Nothing false or misleading was found in the words. The song teaches God's knowledge, providence and presence and rests the believer's peace on them, drawing on Psalm 139, Psalm 23 and Proverbs 3. It is a song of providence rather than the gospel: it names no act of Christ and does not ground its hope of life after death in his cross or resurrection. That is an absence, not an error.

strengths.title: A song for the anxious and the aging
strengths.explanation: The comfort rests on God's knowledge of every circumstance and on his leading through death, so it suits seasons of suffering, doubt and approaching death, and a room can sing it without explanation.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published original key is Bb per PraiseCharts. No chart was read; test the key with the room.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: One short chorus carries the key phrase and returns after the verses, with a brief closing tag. The repetition reinforces the single idea.
communal.assessment: Short chorus, medium-length lines and a calm shape make it easy for a congregation to learn. Judged from the words and structure rather than a chart.

strengths.title: One plain idea
strengths.explanation: Each verse restates that God knows the believer's way, in circumstance, trial and death, so a visitor can follow it at once.

clarity.assessment: Clear in its theme and wording. The one thing a visitor may not hear is the gospel, since Christ is not named.

synthesis.summary: A CityAlight song on God's complete knowledge of the believer's path, his providence over every trial and his leading through death, offered as the ground of peace. Nothing false or misleading was found. It speaks of providence only: Christ and his work are not named, so the gospel is implicit at most.

scriptureReferences.relevance: God knowing every way of the one he has searched - the idea the title carries.
God's presence wherever the believer goes.
Nothing separating the believer from God's love in life or death.

sources.title: All my ways are known to you
sources.establishes: A pastor-writer's commendation: the song celebrates God's omniscience, power and presence and comforts Christians in life and death. Names CityAlight and Only a Holy God.
